newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ROTOR VOLGOGRAD STUMBLE LEAVES WAY OPEN FOR RIVALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROTOR VOLGOGRAD STUMBLE LEAVES WAY OPEN FOR RIVALS.

text.p: Russian league leaders Rotor Volgograd dropped two key points to lowly opponents on Saturday, giving rivals Spartak Moscow a chance to go top with just two games of the season left if they win on Sunday.

Rotor, who have been showing increasing signs of nerves, struggled to a disappointing 0-0 draw away to strugglers Chernomorets Novorossiisk, 14th in the 18-team premier division and just two points clear of the relegation zone.

The result leaves Rotor on 67 points with two games left and Spartak -- champions in 1992, 1993 and 1994 -- will go top if they win their derby match away to Torpedo Moscow on Sunday. Spartak are second with 65 points.
Defending champions Alania Vladikavkaz are in fourth place on 63 points but on Sunday should beat bottom side Lada Togliatti, who are already certain to be relegated.
CSKA Moscow, who started the day in third place on 63 points, virtually ruled themselves out of the title race by losing 2-1 away to mid-table side Baltika Kaliningrad.

Vasily Baranov opened the scoring for the home side in the 55th minute with a tremendous 20-metre volley and substitute Yevgeny Shukanov settled the match seconds after coming on in the 73rd minute, firing home after a goalmouth scramble.
CSKA defender Fereira Leonidas scored from close range in the last minute but by then it was too late.
Dinamo Moscow's faint hopes of sneaking the title also ended, thanks to a 3-2 away defeat to struggling 15th placed KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny.
